sources.title: AFI Catalog: The Shawshank Redemption (1994)
supports: Tim Robbins is credited as Andy Dufresne; the listed distractors play Red, Warden Norton, and Heywood.
Frank Darabont is credited as writer/director, Roger Deakins as cinematographer, and Thomas Newman for music.
The film is based on Stephen King’s 1982 novella ‘Rita Hayworth and the Shawshank Redemption.’
sources.limits: The catalog page labels this 1994 title outside AFI’s core 1893–1993 catalog. Its prison narrative is fictional, not documentary evidence about real prisons.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 67th Academy Awards (1995)
supports: The Shawshank Redemption received seven nominations.
Morgan Freeman was nominated in Actor in a Leading Role.
The ledger also lists nominations for Deakins, Francis-Bruce, Newman, Best Picture, Sound, and Darabont’s adapted screenplay.
sources.limits: The 1995 ceremony honors the 1994 release; it supports award outcomes, not fictional plot propositions.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: The French Connection (1971)
supports: Gene Hackman is credited as Jimmy ‘Popeye’ Doyle; the listed distractors play Charnier, Russo, and Boca.
Don Ellis is credited as music composer and conductor.
AFI records the 1975 sequel with Hackman and Rey.
sources.limits: Do not use the fictionalized screen story as evidence about real police practice. The 1975 sequel is distinct from the 1971 film asked about.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 44th Academy Awards (1972)
supports: The French Connection received eight nominations and five wins.
Gene Hackman won Actor; William Friedkin, Jerry Greenberg, Philip D’Antoni, and Ernest Tidyman won in their listed categories.
Roy Scheider was a supporting-actor nominee; Owen Roizman and the sound team were also nominated.
sources.limits: The 1972 ceremony follows the 1971 release and supports only the listed award outcomes.

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Midnight Cowboy (1969)
supports: Jon Voight is credited as Joe Buck; the other listed candidates play Ratso Rizzo, Cass, and Shirley.
The film adapts James Leo Herlihy’s novel and AFI documents improvisational rehearsal/dialogue exercises by Voight and Hoffman.
AFI records the 1969 X-rated opening and a 1971 re-rating to R.
sources.limits: The dated rating history must be kept distinct from the 1969 release and 1970 Academy ceremony. Characters are fictional.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 42nd Academy Awards (1970)
supports: Midnight Cowboy received seven nominations and three wins.
It won Best Picture, Directing for John Schlesinger, and adapted screenplay for Waldo Salt.
Both Dustin Hoffman and Jon Voight were Actor nominees; Sylvia Miles was a supporting-actress nominee.
sources.limits: The 1970 ledger records ceremony outcomes for the 1969 release, not character facts beyond film identity.

question_sources.film: Born on the Fourth of July

option_mapping.Al Pacino: Associated with an earlier unmade version, not the 1989 finished film

sources.title: AFI Catalog: Born on the Fourth of July (1989)
supports: Tom Cruise is credited as Ron Kovic; Willem Dafoe is Charlie and Kyra Sedgwick is Donna.
The film is based on Ron Kovic’s 1976 autobiography; Oliver Stone and Kovic are credited as writers.
AFI records Cruise’s 1988 casting announcement and an earlier delayed project that had Pacino associated with the lead.
sources.limits: The adaptation includes dramatic reconstruction. Do not equate every film scene with the real Kovic’s biography or confuse Pacino’s earlier unmade-project association with casting in the 1989 film.

sources.organization: Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences
sources.title: The 62nd Academy Awards (1990)
supports: Born on the Fourth of July received eight nominations and two wins.
It won Directing for Oliver Stone and Film Editing for David Brenner and Joe Hutshing.
Tom Cruise was nominated in Actor in a Leading Role; Stone and Kovic were nominated for adapted screenplay.
sources.limits: The 1990 ceremony follows the 1989 release and supports the listed awards only.
